input.prompt: Paint a sibling panel to the reference image, as if by the same Srikalahasti kalamkari artisan on the same bolt of hand-woven cotton. Copy the reference exactly for: the outer border (madder-red band filled with pale ecru-pink dotted lotus blossoms on a scrolling ecru vine, framed by two thin ecru bands of black dots, running around all four edges), the tree's construction (ecru trunk filled with cross-hatching and scales, curling ecru branches outlined in black and edged with rows of dots, a dense dome-shaped canopy of dotted lotus blossoms, lotus buds, green leaves and paisley mango leaves), the iron-black freehand kalam line with slightly irregular weight, and the very high density of hand-drawn fill pattern on every surface. Only the ground colour changes: the field inside the border is dyed deep indigo blue for night, sprinkled with tiny ecru dots. The panel is photographed flat and straight-on and fills the whole frame edge to edge. Composition, symmetrical like a temple cloth: a lush Tree of Life stands in the exact centre on a small dotted mound, its full flowering canopy filling the upper middle of the panel; a crescent moon in turmeric yellow with an ecru inner edge sits above the canopy, and small eight-petalled stars in ecru and yellow are scattered across the indigo sky. LEFT of the tree, beneath a scalloped balcony arch with a carved railing at the bottom: one young woman with long black hair in a long braid, wearing a madder-red saree densely patterned with dots and a striped indigo-and-yellow border, sits on a flat wooden swing hung from the arch by two chains; she holds a small plain dark mobile phone to her ear; beside her on the swing a small striped cat sleeps curled up. RIGHT of the tree, beneath a matching scalloped window arch with lattice shutters: one young man with short black hair, a neat short beard and round thin-rimmed glasses, wearing an ecru kurta patterned with tiny dots, sits at a low wooden desk with one closed book on it, holding a small plain dark mobile phone to his ear. Both figures are drawn in the classical kalamkari manner: faces in side profile turned toward the tree, large elongated almond eyes, long nose, stylised hands with five slender fingers, flat patterned drapery outlined in black, ornaments drawn as dotted lines. A single continuous ecru vine sprouting lotus buds, small green leaves and curling tendrils starts at her phone, rises and winds through the branches of the central tree, and comes down to end at his phone, linking the two. Exactly two people in the whole panel, no other figures. Flat natural vegetable-dye colours only: deep madder red, indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, undyed ecru cotton, iron-black lines. Visible cotton weave texture and slight dye bleed at colour edges. Completely flat: no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism, no clean vector look. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, blank phones. No lamps, no desk lamp, no diyas, no candles, no lanterns, no fire, no flames.
